model.name: Constraint / Requirement Rule
model.purpose: Represent one governed formal or formalizable rule that constrains, requires, permits or prohibits a subject under explicit applicability, authority and evaluation semantics.
model.scope_statement: Owns rule identity and immutable revision; source statement and normalized expression; rule kind, normative modality, severity, priority and criticality; issuer, owner, steward, subject, target, beneficiary and authority; rationale and evidence references; scope, jurisdiction, system boundary, applicability, trigger, preconditions and effective period; predicate, operands, variables, operators, datatypes, units, tolerance, cardinality, quantifiers and logical composition; dependencies and traceability; evaluation input, engine, profile, result and evidence; exceptions, waivers, conflicts and precedence; approval, effectivity, suspension, correction, retirement, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Requirement, policy, standard, control, system, object, actor, decision, test, observation, evidence, exception and enforcement masters remain external.
in_scope: Rule identity, source and normalized expression, kind, modality, revision and authority
Applicability, predicate, operands, datatypes, units, logic, dependency, traceability, evaluation and outcomes
Exceptions, conflicts, lifecycle, provenance, governance, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning stakeholder need, requirement record, policy, standard, control, system, object, actor, decision, test, observation, evidence, exception or enforcement lifecycles

Equating syntax validity with satisfaction, satisfaction with conformance, conformance with compliance, rule-engine output with accountable decision, or normative keyword with authority absent an adopting context
Executing approval, waiver, enforcement, protected disclosure, external system mutation, safety action or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Requirement owns the stakeholder need or governed requirement record. Constraint / Requirement Rule owns a separately reusable formal or formalizable normative expression; the candidate parent signal is held for review.
These authoritative packages may issue or group rules. Their identity, governance and lifecycle remain external while each rule preserves source and authority.
SHACL, JSON Schema and Schematron are executable projections. Schema syntax, engine conformance and validation reports do not replace rule identity or substantive intent.
A rule evaluation supplies a qualified result. Accountable decisions, remedies, sanctions and physical or digital enforcement remain external actions.
Tests and evidence support verification or assessment. A passed test or satisfied predicate does not by itself prove system validation, compliance, safety or legal effect.
The rule records bounded exception references and their effect on evaluation. The external authorization case and accountable approval remain independently mastered.
Engines evaluate pinned projections against input snapshots. Runtime, deployment, code, security and operational lifecycles remain external.

owner_package_requirements: Declare the Dimension owner, rule steward, requirement and policy owners, issuing authorities, evaluators, approvers and disclosure roles.
Register authoritative requirement, policy, standard, control, system, object, test, decision, exception, evidence and enforcement masters.
Publish rule-kind, modality, operator, datatype, unit, outcome, precedence, access, retention and interoperability registries.
Pin domain, model, schema, policy, legal, safety, security, jurisdiction, engine and exchange profiles.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint rule, expression, revision, evaluation, exception, resolution and projection identifiers only in the adopting Dimension namespace; preserve requirement, policy, standard, system, test, decision, evidence and enforcement identities as typed external references.
registry_links: Dimension-local rule, operator, outcome, authority, exception, access, retention and provenance registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative rule identity, rule kind, source statement, immutable revision, applicability profile, issuer and source; never use title, text hash, filename or expression alone as identity.
Keep need, requirement record, constraint rule, policy, control, standard, test, validation result, compliance assessment, decision, exception, waiver and enforcement action distinct.
patch_rules: Additive extensions use a Dimension-owned namespace and declare target node, domain profile, authority, source, rationale, access, time, engine and interoperability impact.
Breaking changes require a new version, migration and crosswalk maps, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior rule revisions, evaluations and exceptions.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when identity, kind, modality, predicate, applicability, authority, lifecycle, evaluation and access meaning remain intact.

SysML, OCL, SBVR, DMN, SHACL, OWL, SPARQL, ODRL, LegalRuleML, XACML, JSON Schema, Schematron, OSCAL, OpenAPI and Rego mappings pin source and target versions and declare transformed, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the rule and immutable expression revision.
Governed globally resolvable rule, requirement or policy IRI.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z; keep issue, approval, effective, evaluation, exception, suspension, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {rule-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-evaluation-id}; never use a date, title, expression, result, filename or hash alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, source and vocabulary versions, rule and applicability scope, clocks, provenance, assurance, license, engine and access marking for each retained serial artifact.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may issue, formalize, classify, approve, activate, evaluate, waive, resolve, revise, disclose, retain and tombstone rules.
Every assertion requires rule identity and revision, kind, modality, subject, applicability, source, authority, state, evidence and lineage as applicable.
Agents never infer substantive correctness, legal force, conformance, compliance, safety or accountable approval from syntactic validity, a rule-engine outcome or one source alone.
Requirements, policies, standards, controls, systems, tests, decisions, evidence, exceptions and enforcement remain external masters.

Automated agents may append low-risk formalizations, validations and projections under delegation, but approval, waiver, enforcement, protected disclosure and irreversible deletion require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, requested revision, rule kind, applicability, effective horizon, assurance, engine, license and access policy; return the minimum permitted projection.
create: Create stable identity, source statement, rule kind, issuer, authority, subject, applicability and explicit unknowns before adding formal execution semantics.
update: Append an immutable expression, applicability, approval, evaluation, exception, resolution or correction revision with actor, authority, reason, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply safety, legal, policy, dispute, audit, retention and legal-hold rules; tombstone eligible Rule-owned records or withdraw projections while preserving identity, material provenance and non-cascading external references.

roles.name: Dimension owner
responsibilities: Own namespace, mastership, delegation, access, retention and federation rules.

roles.name: Rule steward
responsibilities: Own rule identity, kinds, operators, lifecycle, version and crosswalk policy.

roles.name: Issuer or requirement owner
responsibilities: Own source intent, authority, applicability, rationale and approval request.

roles.name: Domain or vocabulary steward
responsibilities: Own referenced terms, datatypes, units, value sets and profiles.

roles.name: Rule author or formalizer
responsibilities: Own normalized expression, mappings, test fixtures and declared semantic limits.

roles.name: Evaluator or engine authority
responsibilities: Own input snapshot, engine, profile, evaluation trace and result assertion.

roles.name: Approver or exception authority
responsibilities: Own effectivity, waiver, deviation, conflict resolution and accountable decisions.

roles.name: Reviewer or auditor
responsibilities: Review authority, consistency, results, conflicts, corrections, access and retention without rewriting originals.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and sensitive disclosure unless active Dimension, role, purpose, rule sensitivity, jurisdiction, license and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.
exceptions: Emergency or legally compelled access must be grounded, time-limited, purpose-bound, attributable, independently reviewed and unable to erase immutable rule, evaluation, exception or legal-hold evidence.
audit_requirements: Log actor, role, purpose, rule and revision identity, action, decision, policy, engine and vocabulary versions, RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, affected fields, source evidence and outcome for privileged mutation or disclosure.

read_order: Read the nearest Dimension-owner AGENTS.md, issuing and exception authorities, active domain, policy, jurisdiction, time, access, retention and licensing rules.
Read this model AGENTS.md, pinned spec.yaml and required requirement, policy, standard, control, system, test, decision, evidence and enforcement instructions before mutation.

coverage.claim: Source-grounded reviewable draft covering Constraint / Requirement Rule identity, source and normalized expression, kind, modality, authority, applicability, predicate, composition, traceability, evaluation, outcomes, exceptions, conflicts, lifecycle, governance and interoperability.

checklist.notes: Rule, expression revision, evaluation, exception, resolution and successor identities remain distinct.
Requirement, constraint, invariant, business, validation, policy and legal rule profiles are explicit.
Expression, modality, subject, scope, predicate, operands, logic, severity, state and outcome are covered.
Input snapshots, engine traces, tests, evidence and evaluations remain independently identified.
Draft, proposed, approved, effective, suspended, superseded and retired states preserve history.
Requirements, policies, standards, controls, systems, tests, decisions, exceptions and evidence use typed references.
Issue, approval, effective, evaluation, waiver, suspension, correction and ingestion clocks remain distinct.
Jurisdiction, system boundary, environment and location scope are represented where relevant.
Issuer, source, rationale, formalization, approval, evaluation, exception, conflict resolution and revision are linked.
Rule ownership, requirement ownership, system responsibility, evaluation authority and enforcement authority are not conflated.
Identity, expression, applicability, type, unit, logic, engine, outcome, exception and crosswalk checks are explicit.
Role, purpose, policy sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Corrections, disputes, exceptions, audit or legal hold, withdrawal and tombstones are non-cascading.
Requirements, modeling, rule, schema, policy, control and API mappings disclose loss.
Registration, formalization, classification, applicability, composition, activation, evaluation, exception, revision and projection declare controlled effects.

known_omissions: Domain, safety, legal, policy, security, privacy, jurisdiction, engine, licensing and retention profiles require expert review.
Requirements, policies, standards, controls, systems, objects, tests, decisions, evidence, exceptions and enforcement lifecycles remain neighboring masters.
Universal satisfiability, conflict resolution, theorem proving, optimization, code generation, autonomous enforcement and legal-effect determination remain future work.
conflicts: Requirement, constraint, invariant, business rule, validation shape, policy rule and legal norm use different authority and evaluation semantics and require a profile.
Closed-world validation, open-world inference, three-valued logic, defeasible legal reasoning and policy combining cannot share one universal outcome model.
Syntactic validity, rule satisfaction, verification, validation, conformance, compliance, safety and legal effect are distinct governed claims.
regional_assumptions: ISO and OMG engineering sources do not define every legal, business, data-quality or access-policy rule.
LegalRuleML and XACML are legal-norm and authorization-policy profiles rather than universal constraint languages.
Authority, waiver, enforcement, compliance, retention and legal consequences depend on organization, domain and jurisdiction.
adversarial_checks: Reject a rule without stable identity, revision, source expression, kind, modality, subject, applicability, issuer, authority and lineage.
Reject a requirement record, policy artifact, standard, control, test, validation result, decision, exception or enforcement action represented as the rule itself.
Reject executable evaluation without pinned rule revision, input snapshot, engine, profile, clock, outcome vocabulary and trace.
Reject passed syntax or validation as proof of conformance, compliance, safety, legal force or substantive correctness.
Reject exception or precedence without scope, authority, rationale, conditions, effective time and expiry.
Reject silent last-write-wins when rules or evaluations conflict; preserve both sources and the qualified resolution.
Reject approval, waiver, enforcement, protected disclosure or record destruction outside delegated authority.
